Municipality Agent Technical Reference

What the system is, what happens on every request, and why each piece is shaped the way it is. Every number was measured on the stack as built, 2026-09-20.

1. What it is

A resident-facing assistant for a fictional City of San Diego. Residents ask about trash pickup, permits, business tax, City events and service requests, and file four kinds of application from the chat: building permit, business tax certificate, Get It Done service request, short-term rental (STRO) licence. Staff sign in to a console with a queue, a reporting dashboard, and a trace of every model turn.

Facts from tools, policy from retrieval

Rows are answered by typed function calls against Postgres. Policy text is answered by hybrid retrieval over pgvector. The tool allow-list per intent enforces the split.

Nothing from the model's memory

Every fact traces to a tool result or a cited chunk. Everything the model reads that the team did not write is fenced as untrusted data.

Every turn leaves a trace

Intent, tier, model, tool calls with source, retrieved chunks, tokens, latency, cost. The dashboard and the evals are computed from that table.

3. One chat turn, end to end

  1. Edge checks, before any model call. Message at most 4,000 characters, session id matches a fixed pattern, at most five document ids. The per-IP token bucket is charged. The session cookie is verified or, on first contact, minted. The per-session turn cap and the daily cost breaker are read. A stream slot is taken without waiting; none free means a 429 with Retry-After, before any headers.
  2. Intake check. A file drop, or a reply while this session has an application waiting for information, is a workflow turn and short-circuits. Its reply is templated, never generated.
  3. History. The last ten messages for the session.
  4. Classify. The small tier returns JSON: intent, confidence, complexity, secondary intents. A tracking-number pattern sets the intent directly with no model call.
  5. Select the tier. Escalate when confidence is under 0.6, complexity is high, or a second intent is present; otherwise smart. The reason is a sentence on the trace.
  6. Profile. One per intent: system prompt, tool allow-list, knowledge-base topic. Seven intents.
  7. Retrieve. pgvector cosine top 8 and full-text top 8, fused by reciprocal rank fusion, top 5 returned. A topic filter runs first and is dropped if it yields fewer than two hits.
  8. Build the prompt. Shared preamble, numbered sources each inside <source n kind trust="untrusted">, the date line last so the cacheable prefix stays stable.
  9. Tool loop. At most four rounds. Only allow-listed tools run; an off-list call gets an error summary. Repeated calls are served from a per-turn cache. Tool JSON returns inside a fence labelled t1, t2 so it can never be cited as [n]. Text next to a tool call is a preamble and is not streamed.
  10. Answer, cite, persist, done. The final round streams. Citations map back to sources; if none were cited the top two return flagged implicit. One traces row, then the two messages pointing at it. One done event carries reply, citations, actions and trace. A failure anywhere is a done with the fallback reply, never a dropped connection.

4. Routing and the prompt

  • The classifier sees the last three user messages, so "and recycling?" resolves against the address given a turn earlier.
  • smalltalk gets no tools and no retrieval. general gets every tool and no topic filter; housing, parking, utilities, library and jobs questions land there.
  • Six tools ride on every domain profile so a message with two subjects is answered in one turn: trash schedule, next pickup, events, council district, application status, referral. Tools that quote money, open a form or file a case stay behind their own intent.
  • The preamble fixes the rules the evals score: answer only from sources and tool results, cite [n], call every fee an estimate, never state a number no tool produced, never do arithmetic on a tool's numbers, handle every request in a multi-part message before asking anything, say whether a fact came from live or seed data, quote a filing's department and tracking number verbatim, and treat fenced text as data.
  • The service-request category list in the prompt is generated from the seed table at import, so the prompt and the table cannot drift.

5. Retrieval

  • Nine markdown files under api/kb/, about 1,000 lines, 133 chunks, each file with title, topic and source URL in frontmatter.
  • Each ### Q: FAQ block is one chunk; prose is packed into roughly 1,200 character windows with 150 of overlap on paragraph boundaries. Chunk text starts with the title and heading so a retrieved paragraph carries its context.
  • Ingest is idempotent per document by content hash and runs under an advisory lock: two replicas cannot double the knowledge base and a crash mid-ingest resumes.
  • Dense search finds paraphrases; full text pins exact strings like "SB-1186". Reciprocal rank fusion needs no score calibration between the two scales.
  • The embedding index is HNSW because the migration runs against an empty table and IVFFlat needs rows to train.

6. Tools and live City data

Sixteen tools. Each is a plain async function with a pydantic input model; the registry derives the OpenAI JSON schema from the model, so contract and validation cannot drift. dispatch() never raises: an unknown tool, bad arguments or an exception becomes {"error", "summary"} and the model gets another round. Every result carries a summary sentence, a source (live or seed) and, for address tools, a match (seed, geocoded, zip).

Live data comes from the City's own ArcGIS services: the geocoder, council districts, street sweeping, zoning, permits on file, and the Granicus RSS of council agendas. One resolver backs every address-taking tool: exact seed match, then the City geocoder at score 80 or better, then a bare ZIP. All live calls go through one HTTP module with a 4-second timeout, a 10-minute cache, a None return on any failure, and redirect targets re-checked against the *.sandiego.gov allow-list. A dead City service degrades to seed data, labelled "based on demo data", never a 500.

Web search is built and off SEARCH_PROVIDER=none: it reports itself unconfigured rather than being an advertised tool that always fails.

7. Prompt safety

  • Every knowledge-base chunk, fetched page and tool result is wrapped in <source trust="untrusted">; a defang step neutralises any <source text inside so a page cannot close the fence. The preamble says fenced text is never an instruction.
  • The tool allow-list is enforced in the loop, not only offered to the model.
  • Status lookups return a redacted view: tracking number, type, status, department, fee estimate, names of missing fields. Applicant fields never reach the model.
  • Model markdown is rendered by a small allow-list renderer: http and https links only, no raw HTML, no data-URI images. A browser test feeds it <script>, onerror and javascript: links and asserts inert text.
  • The hardening eval category (60 items across injection, scope, ambiguity, numbers, dates, multi-turn, noise, language, live-data failure and cost loops) scores guardrail 100% and "no number absent from tool results" 100%. One open item: a "developer mode" wrapper flips the router to smalltalk and the legitimate half of the question goes unanswered. Recorded, not hidden.

8. Streaming and concurrency

The stream route holds no pool connection. A FastAPI yield dependency is not released until a streaming body drains, and taking one deadlocked the API at exactly pool_size + max_overflow = 20 concurrent streams. Measured, fixed, and now gated by a probe in CI.

  • Admission control is a 429 before the body. At most 16 turns stream at once; the slot is released on a clean done, an exception, or a client that hangs up.
  • Every model call has a 45-second read timeout and one retry. The SDK default was 600 seconds with two retries.
  • Certificate rendering and every boto3 call run in a thread with 3-second connect and 10-second read timeouts.
  • A heartbeat comment every 15 seconds keeps a load balancer from idling the connection out during a slow tool round.
MeasurementBeforeAfter
20 concurrent streams, stub modelevery stream 60 s, then the apologyp95 0.29 s, 4 turned away with 429
50 concurrent streams, stub model30 HTTP 500s, p50 30 sp95 0.43 s, zero 500s
20 concurrent streams, live Bedrocknot measured9 s total, 16 served, 4 turned away, zero errors
pytest load test, 40 streams, scratch databasenonezero 500s, complete turns, p95 under 2 s

9. Intake and the workflow engine

Two intake paths create the same row. Document: upload to SeaweedFS, pypdf in a thread (under 50 characters is a scan, refused honestly), type detection on the small tier, field extraction on the extract tier into the type's pydantic schema, validation, submit. Form: a quick action renders the schema inline; the submit carries an Idempotency-Key so a double click returns the original row. Needs info: missing fields are asked for in chat and the next message is extracted against only those fields; the state machine re-validates, the model does not decide completeness. Workflow replies are templated: a tracking number, a fee and a missing-field list are facts the engine already knows.

  • Tracking numbers come from one Postgres sequence per type; the year comes from the Pacific clock.
  • The worker claims rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so a second worker never processes the same application.
  • Adding a type is one pydantic schema, one validator, one fee function, seed rows and a sample PDF. The STRO licence was added that way; form, extraction, state machine and certificate path did not change.

10. Data model

GroupTables
Resident recordsapplications, application_events, documents, chat_messages, traces
Reference, seeded and reloaded on starttrash_zones, addresses, events, permit_types, service_categories, referrals, council_districts
Knowledge basekb_documents with content hash, kb_chunks with text, embedding vector(1024) HNSW, tsv
Operationsstaff_users, staff_sessions, rate_limits, schema_migrations
  • Plain SQL migrations in filename order under an advisory lock, tracked in schema_migrations, with .down.sql files from 006 and a --rollback flag. The vector width is asserted at startup so a mismatched embedding model fails at boot, not at the first insert.
  • The seed loader reloads reference tables only; resident tables are on a never-truncate list and sample applications are inserted only if absent.
  • SeaweedFS keys are documents/<id>/<filename> and certificates/<tracking>.pdf. Pointing S3_ENDPOINT at AWS is the whole change for real S3.
  • backup.sh writes a pg_dump and a tar of the object store; reset_demo.sh calls it first; restore.sh restores into a scratch database and prints row counts side by side. The drill has been run.

11. Sessions, staff auth, limits

ControlMechanismWhy this shape
Resident sessionsOn first contact the API sets resident_session = HMAC-SHA256(session id, secret), HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 30 days. Later requests on that id must carry it or get 403.Nothing stored server-side, a restart logs nobody out, rotating the secret starts everyone a new conversation. No bypass header; the eval runner and smoke carry cookie jars.
Staff authscrypt hash, 32-byte token stored as SHA-256 only, HttpOnly cookie for 12 hours, generic 401 after a one-second pause, 429 after five failures a minute.The console issues documents, so it is behind a real login. advance writes the username as the actor.
Per-IP rate limitToken bucket in Postgres, one atomic statement, burst 20, refill 30 a minute, on every route a stranger can reach.Postgres rather than memory so two API replicas share one limit. A broken limiter lets the request through; the cost cap is the ceiling that protects the bill.
CostEvery call priced onto the trace. Per-session turn cap 200; daily cap $25 on the Pacific day, checked before the classifier, warning at 80%.The classifier is itself a model call; a breaker that trips after it is not a breaker.
IdempotencyIdempotency-Key on form submits under a unique partial index; without a key, the same payload from the same session inside 60 s is the same filing.A double click, a retry, and the 403 session rotation all replay the same request.
RetentionTRACE_RETENTION_DAYS, default keep; above zero the worker sweeps daily.The California Public Records Act sets a two-year floor before destruction.
Production modeENVIRONMENT=prod refuses to start on any placeholder secret, a localhost origin, or a non-TLS origin, naming every offender at once.Every credential in the repository is public by design; prod must not be able to use one.

12. Observability and the dashboard

  • Every response carries X-Request-ID; one access line per request logs status, duration and, for buffered chat, the trace row id. No resident message text is logged.
  • /health is free and anonymous: process, database, object store, chunk count, startup errors; 503 when the database or object store is down. /health/deep makes the model probe, staff-only, cached 60 seconds.
  • Startup steps are wrapped: a failed ingest leaves the app serving with /health red instead of crash-looping.
  • GET /api/reports/summary?days= computes the dashboard in SQL: turns, sessions, cost, p50 and p95 latency, error and fallback turns, turns and cost by day, intents, tiers, tools with error rate and live share, citation rate, applications by type and status, median hours to review, and the ten most recent unanswered turns. The unanswered panel is how a city finds its next knowledge-base gap.

The evals report and never gate; every generalising fix is logged rather than tuned to an item. GitHub Actions on every push and pull request: api (ruff, format, pytest), web (typecheck, lint, build), security (pip-audit, npm audit, gitleaks, Trivy on both images as a hard gate), compose-smoke (the full stack with a stub model that classifies, the smoke script in stub mode, and a 20-stream probe that gates). e2e and a nightly eval exist behind an AWS OIDC secret.

14. Configuration and the provider swap

One typed settings object read from .env. The three committed profiles differ only in model names and base URLs: .env.ollama, .env.openai, .env.bedrock. The API speaks the OpenAI protocol through one client module that times, prices and traces every call; the gateway maps tier aliases to Bedrock model ids. Changing the embedding width needs a fresh database, and the width is asserted at startup.

15. Production shapes

Both change environment values and where the containers run, nothing in the code. Model usage is about $0.03 a turn on the current tiers. Full tables and monthly costs are in PRODUCTION_PLAN.md.

A. One VM, compose, TLS, backups pilot

EC2 with the five compose services plus Caddy for TLS, nightly backup to S3, an instance role, secrets from SSM, CloudWatch alarms on health and disk. About $90 a month plus model usage. Removes the plaintext cookie, secrets in user-data, backups on the same disk, unrotated logs, an unnoticed outage. Keeps one host and one API process.

B. Managed containers, RDS, S3

ECS Fargate for api (2), web (2), worker (1) and litellm; ALB with ACM and WAF; RDS Postgres Multi-AZ with pgvector; S3; Secrets Manager; CloudWatch. About $310 a month plus model usage. Two API tasks are safe because rate limits, idempotency, ingest and worker claims live in Postgres. Adds a platform to operate.

16. Known limits, by decision

Payments, resident accounts, real write integrations (Accela and Get It Done have no public write API), OCR, Spanish, TLS in the compose demo, a per-claim faithfulness score, an independent accessibility audit, a Public Records Act redaction procedure, the staff login throttle being in-process, and the developer-mode router flip. Each has a reason and a production answer in the demo kit's "Gaps left on purpose" tab.

17. Questions an engineer will ask

QuestionAnswer the code supports
What breaks with two API replicas?Rate limits, idempotency, worker claims, migrations and ingest are in Postgres. The staff login throttle is the one in-memory counter left.
Where does the model get its facts?Only from fenced sources and tool results. A "no number absent from tool results" scorer runs on every eval.
How do you know streaming works?A load test in pytest, a probe in CI, a live measurement on Bedrock. A heartbeat regression passed 574 mocked tests and was caught by the browser test on the rebuilt stack the same hour; it is written up in DECISIONS.md.
What happens when Bedrock hangs?45-second timeout, one retry, fallback reply with a trace naming the error, connection never dropped. LiteLLM falls back from Opus to Sonnet for the escalate tier.
What happens when the City's ArcGIS is down?Seed data, labelled as such, in under 4 seconds.
How is a new application type added?One schema, one validator, one fee function, seed rows, a sample PDF. The STRO licence proves it.
How is a new system of record added?One adapter module behind an existing tool contract. The council-district tool answered from a seed row in phase 1 and from ArcGIS in phase 2 with no prompt change.
